text:
maya: Quick q — we're hitting a bunch of flaky matches in gateway when host and path both match different services. Thinking of adding a 'service-binding' anchor so we can pin certain hosts to a service before other match heuristics run. Thoughts?

ben: Do you mean a syntactic anchor in the route match DSL, or a deploy-time binding?

maya: DSL. Example idea: add `service:!myservice` or `bind_service: myservice` on a route so host/path matching short-circuits if the bind exists. That way customers can opt-in when they really want deterministic host->svc mapping.

aleks: I like opt-in. My worry is interactions with header overrides and weighted fallbacks. If we short-circuit, how do we honor `x-svc-fallback` header?

maya: Good call. Proposal: precedence order: 1) explicit service binding (if present) 2) header-driven override 3) host+path matcher scoring 4) stable fallback weights. Bindings would still be overridable by a higher-priority deploy policy (enterprise), but not by ad-hoc headers unless `allow_header_override: true` is set on the binding.

katie: Can we show this in console UX? If a binding exists we should surface a small badge and a tooltip: "Pinned to myservice — headers won't override unless allowed". Saves support noise.

ben: Also think about telemetry. We need a metric for "binding_hits" vs "binding_violations" (header tried to override but denied). That helps evaluate if bindings are useful.

maya: Agreed. Simple counters + trace tag on routed requests: `route_binding=explicit|none|denied-header`. Then customers can filter in Console for routing regressions.

aleks: Edgecase: what if path matcher for `myservice` has a capture like `/org/:orgId/*` and another service has `/org/*/billing`. Binding might make things less flexible. We should warn on binding creation if existing match specificity is lower than conflicting routes.

maya: Good point. We'll run a pre-apply check and warn: "Binding may shadow {n} routes with higher specificity" and require `--force` in CLI or a confirmation in Console.

katie: UX wording: avoid technical terms. "Pin this host to a specific service — may affect some existing routes" with a link to docs.

ben: Implementation note: runtime should evaluate binding first as a hash lookup (host -> service) then fall back to matcher tree. So perf is actually better for bound hosts.

aleks: For config format suggestion, maybe keep it compact, e.g.:
```
match:
  host: "acme.example.com"
  path: "/org/:orgId/*"
bind_service: "accounts-service"
allow_header_override: false
```

maya: That looks good. Also include `binding_scope: global|team|org` for multi-tenant customers.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/route-binding-optin -> test/staging (sha: abcd1234) :rocket:

katie: One more ask — add a lint rule that flags bindings created without an associated unit test or routing smoke test. Too many silent breakages otherwise.

maya: Will add lint + console warning + telemetry. If no objections, I'll draft a short RFC and a small console mock for product review.

ben: +1 from infra side. Please include migration guidance for existing hosts that relied on header overrides.

aleks: +1 from runtime. We should also publish a best-practices doc for when to use binding vs matcher tuning.

maya: Cool — I'll draft and ping everyone for review. Thanks! :thumbsup:
